newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch minister welcomes extra British cattle cull.
newsitem.headline: Dutch minister welcomes extra British cattle cull.

text.p: Britain's decision on Monday to go ahead with a selective slaughter of cattle most at risk from mad cow disease was welcomed by Dutch farm minister Jozias Van Aartsen, whose country is next to take over the EU presidency.
Britain announced in a major u-turn that it would slaughter around 100,000 more cattle in a bid to persuade the European Union to lift its six-month-old worldwide ban on British beef exports.
"It's excellent news and just what I expected," Van Aartsen told Reuters after the first day of a two-day EU farm ministers meeting.
Van Aartsen, whose country takes over the rotating EU presidency on January 1, 1997, said London must now come forward with ideas on how the ban on British beef exports could be gradually lifted.
"We will discuss during the Dutch presidency lifting the ban in stages," he said.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler earlier on Monday ruled out any speedy lifting of the ban.
"I think we need to move forward step by step as agreed," he told a news conference before the British announcement.
German Farm Minister Jochen Borchert wast cautious.
"For the moment, I don't see any possibility for a regional relaxation or for certain products," Borchert told Reuters earlier. "It will take time."
A selective cull was agreed by British Prime Minister John Major with other EU heads of government at the EU Florence summit last June as part of a package to end the crisis over mad cow disease.
But Major scrapped the plan in September after new scientific evidence that the disease -- Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) -- would die out by 2001 under existing measures.
British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg is due to brief his EU counterparts on Tuesday on the selective cull and progress in eradicating the disease, but no decisions will be taken.
